channel.title: Lokesh Ram Chand — Portfolio — Blog
channel.description: A dedicated software engineer building intelligent, scalable platforms. I combine modern full-stack development with machine learning technologies to architect comprehensive, production-ready solutions.

item.title: Setting Up an Open Source Repo So Contributors Know What to Do
item.description: My PR to accesscraft adds issue forms, contribution policies and CI automation. None of it is code, and all of it decides whether people can contribute.

item.title: Teaching a Link Checker That Not Every GitHub URL Is a Repo
item.description: cncf/automation's link checker marked valid GitHub pages like /sponsors and /topics as broken. I made it double-check against github.com before reporting a 404.

item.title: A Secret-Redaction Fix That Redacted the Secret Out of Existence
item.description: The KubeVirt cloud runner in cncf/automation hid its JIT config so well that the runner never received it. I made it substitute the value again and still keep it out of the logs.

item.title: One Flag Was Printing a Runner Secret Into CI Logs
item.description: The OCI cloud runner in cncf/automation ran its start script with bash -x, which traced the GitHub Actions JIT config into the logs. Removing one flag fixed it.

item.title: When a Profiling Archive Includes Nodes It Never Reached
item.description: Birdwatcher's pprof command archived 0-byte entries for unreachable Milvus nodes and printed the same success message for them. Here's my fix.

item.title: A Typo That Hid a Whole Command, and the Crash Behind It
item.description: Birdwatcher's verify-segment command was fully written but never registered, because its method was named VerifySegmentCommnad. Fixing the typo exposed a startup panic.

item.title: A silent backward-compatibility bug in Apicurio Registry's XSD checker
item.description: A code comment said this case was already handled. It wasn't, and I only found out because a sibling method handled the same case properly.

item.title: Three Goroutines, One Error Variable, and a Restore That Lied
item.description: Birdwatcher's load-backup could report success while dropping keys, because worker goroutines raced on a shared err. I replaced the pattern with errgroup.

item.title: Why 5.0 Wasn't an Integer in Apicurio's Prompt Templates
item.description: An integer prompt-template variable with a default of 5.0 failed its own type check in Apicurio Registry, because Jackson reads every decimal literal as a Double.

item.title: Auditing My Own Portfolio Like Someone Else's Codebase
item.description: I ran a security and production audit on this site. It found an XSS hole in the blog, two vulnerable dependencies, a dead permalink and missing security headers.

item.title: When Success Doesn't Mean It Worked
item.description: A repair command in Birdwatcher, Milvus's diagnostic tool, could report success while writing corrupted protobuf bytes to etcd. Here's how I found and fixed it.

item.title: One Kubeconfig, Unlimited Goroutines: Bounding Meshery's Context Registration
item.description: Meshery spawned one unbounded goroutine per Kubernetes context in an uploaded kubeconfig. I capped it with a semaphore so one request can't exhaust the server.

item.title: The Bug That Wasn't a Bug Yet: Hunting a Dormant API Contract Violation in Meshery
item.description: I read Meshery's naming-convention doc closely and found 20 handlers that would break pagination the day the frontend moved to generated clients.

item.title: The Stub That Made Birdwatcher's Restore Write Nothing
item.description: FileAuditKV.MultiSave in Birdwatcher always returned 'not implemented'. That broke one repair command outright and made restore silently write zero keys.

item.title: A Validator That Crashed Instead of Saying No
item.description: pymilvus's binary-vector check raised a raw TypeError on None values instead of returning False. Swapping two lines fixed it.

item.title: Hardening a 15-Phase AI API for Pre-Production
item.description: What my pre-production audit of Velar found: zero indexes, a root container, a concurrency race, and two security bumps that broke things.

item.title: Deleting One Environment Shouldn't Delete a Shared API Key
item.description: A Postgres trigger in Nango hard-deleted an API key whenever any of its environments was removed, even if the key still belonged to others. I made it relation-aware.

item.title: A Flaky Test That Was Really a Same-Millisecond Bug
item.description: roster's v1 to v2 HITL migration refused valid history whenever two events landed in the same millisecond. The ledger already had a sequence number that fixed it.

item.title: Why I Didn't Just Use ChatGPT for Transaction Parsing
item.description: I put three cheap, deterministic layers in front of the LLM in Velar, and gave the pipeline permission to say 'I don't know.'

item.title: Building a Grounded RAG Pipeline for Financial Data with Milvus and Ollama
item.description: How I kept Velar's explanations local and grounded: Ollama for embeddings and generation, Milvus for lookup, and an early return when there's nothing to ground on.

item.title: Designing a Memory State Machine for ML Predictions
item.description: How I made merchant trust an explicit state in Velar, the race condition I almost shipped, and the decay question I still haven't answered.

item.title: Building an Nginx Configuration I Could Actually Maintain
item.description: How my reverse proxy config went from one fragile file to something I can change without fear, and the reload mistake I kept making.

item.title: Owning the Stack: Building My Personal Cloud
item.description: Why I built my own cloud on Proxmox, and what I learned getting a static IP, a reverse proxy, Keycloak and monitoring running at home.
